decisions.why: The Latin says 'I loved' with no object, and a perfect beside a future (the Greek has the same: ἠγάπησα … εἰσακούσεται). Who or what is loved is left open, and so is *quóniam*: 'because' or 'that'. MS1932 supplies the object (*Amo o Senhor*), which is the Hebrew family's reading and closes the openness. Ruled: *Amei*, bare, the Latin's tense; *porque* as DRB 'because'. The strangeness of loving because of a future hearing is the Latin's own.

decisions.why: The *inférnus* row is open and flagged for Gustavo (D22): the blind reader of Ps 6 heard the hell of the damned first. In the Office of the Dead the Christian overtone is read on purpose.

decisions.why: The soul is *tu*. Two forms of the vocative stand in the psalter: *minha alma* (41:6, settled D42) and *ó minha alma* (102:1, 103:1, the *Bénedic, ánima mea* row). The build here is 102:1's — imperative, vocative, complement — and without *ó* the bare *Volta minha alma* can be heard as 'he turns my soul back' (*volta* is also the third person). Ruled: *ó minha alma*.

decisions.why: The Vespers antiphon of the Office of the Dead (DO Commune C9: *Placébo Dómino * in regióne vivórum*, the asterisk where the verse has it, so the verse reads as the antiphon unchanged). The Latin's word is *régio* (χώρα), not *terra* (γῆ) as in 26:13 *in terra vivéntium* → *na terra dos vivos*; by D15's test two Greek words keep two Portuguese words. *Placére + dative → agradar a* is settled (D44, the row names this verse). Liturgy in Brazil, checked 2026-09-23: the CNBB Liturgia das Horas (Hebrew-based, Ps 114[116A]) reads 9 as *Andarei na presença de Deus, junto a ele na terra dos vivos* (liturgiadashoras.online, fetched), which is also the responsorial refrain sung at Mass (24th Sunday B, per music sites found by search) — a Hebrew-family line (אֶתְהַלֵּךְ), so no witness of the Latin's *Placébo*. MS1932 has *Agradarei ao Senhor na região dos vivos*. **Unverified:** no printed Brazilian pre-conciliar Office of the Dead wording of the antiphon was found on the web; DO's own Portuguese C9 has *Agradarei ao Senhor * na região dos vivos*, which is no evidence (D12).

options.note: DRB 'land'; the phrase Brazilian ears know from 26:13 and the CNBB refrain; merges *régio* with *terra*

decisions.why: The *benefácere* row (56:3 *ao Deus que me fez bem*; 48:19 *quando lhe fizeres bem*) gives *fazer bem*; this verse is named in the row. The stylist hears *te fez bem* as therapeutic ('was good for you', as a walk *faz bem*) and asks for the article. The ambiguity reader heard 'has been good to you' first, 'made you well' second. Ruled: the row, so the three places stay one wording; *te fez o bem* is proposed in the glossary as the row's alternative, to be taken in all three at once if Gustavo prefers it.

decisions.latin: óculos meos a lácrimis, * pedes meos a lapsu
decisions.why: The stylist marks the proparoxytone *lágrimas* at the mediant as the psalm's worst line and asks to front the complements. Refused: the Latin's own mediant is the proparoxytone *lácrimis*; the fronting is inversion for its own sake (rule 5); and the second colon is 55:13's *os meus pés da queda* word for word, which the inversion would break.

choices.114:1: *vocem oratiónis meæ → a voz da minha oração* (the *orátio* row). *exaudíre → escutar* (D3). The subject moved before the verb so that *escutará* takes the mediant; *porque escutará o Senhor* would hear *o Senhor* as the object.
choices.114:2: *inclináre aurem* → *inclinou para mim o seu ouvido*, the third person of the formula row (*inclinai para mim o vosso ouvido*, 16:6, 30:3). The Monday Vespers antiphon *Inclinávit Dóminus * aurem suam mihi* (DO Psalmi major, grep) adds *Dóminus*; as an antiphon it would read *O Senhor inclinou * para mim o seu ouvido*.
choices.114:3a: First colon = 17:5a word for word (*Cercaram-me as dores da morte*), as the Latin is identical (rule 6). *periculum → perigo*, the plain cognate.
choices.114:3b: The Latin's order (object first, verb at the mediant) is kept: it holds *encontrei* at the same place as *encontraram* at the end of 3a, and it avoids the *dor / Senhor* rhyme at mediant and final that the plain order makes (decision `inven`). *invocávi → invoquei*, the *invocáre* row; the second colon is in natural order.
choices.114:4b: *líbera → livrai* (the *liberáre* row; safe under rule 3, past *livrei*). *miserétur → tem piedade* (the *miseréri* row); the family link with *misericordioso* is lost, as in every Portuguese version. *O Dómine* → *Ó Senhor*, the interjection kept.
choices.114:7: *convértere → voltar* (the row; here the soul's turning back, not conversion). *réquies → repouso* (the row, 94:11; MS1932). *benefácere → fazer bem* (the row; 56:3 *ao Deus que me fez bem*; the row names this verse).
choices.114:8: Near-twin of 55:13 *Quóniam eripuísti ánimam meam de morte, et pedes meos de lapsu*: its words are copied (*arrancar* with a source named, the *erípere* row; *lapsus → queda*, D44, which names this verse), with the person changed to the Latin's third (*erípuit*; the Hebrew has the second — not followed). *lácrimæ → lágrimas* (the row). The proparoxytone *lágrimas* at the mediant mirrors the Latin's own *lácrimis*; accepted.
choices.114:9: = the Office of the Dead Vespers antiphon (see decision `regione`).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps114.md (no Diurnal-specific concern: it is printed, Hebrew-based). Formulas copied: 17:5a (114:3a), 55:13 (114:8), the *inclína aurem* row (114:2), 102:1's vocative (114:7). Glossary rows applied: *exaudíre*, *orátio*, *invocáre*, *inférnus* (open, kept), *liberáre*, *miseréri*, *custodíre*, *párvuli*, *humiliáre*, *convértere*, *réquies*, *benefácere*, *erípere*, *lácrimæ*, *lapsus*, *placére* + dative. Liturgical use checked by grep in DO: 114:9 is the Vespers antiphon of the Office of the Dead (C9); 114:2 gives the Monday Vespers antiphon. Brazilian circulation checked on the web (decision `regione`). Hard readings: the objectless *Diléxi*; *Custódiens* without a finite verb; the *invenérunt / invéni* echo.

Hard checks pass (ids 114:1–9 with 3a, 3b, 4b; every mark). Soft length flags accepted: 114:3b first colon −4 (*Tribulação e dor encontrei* — the Latin needs thirteen syllables for three words; one breath either way); 114:4b ‡ colon +4 (*misericordioso* is six syllables for four, and the copula is supplied — D2); 114:7b −3 (*te fez bem*, the benefácere row). The proparoxytone *lágrimas* before * in 114:8 mirrors the Latin *lácrimis*. No rhyme flags (the plain order of 3b would have made *dor / Senhor*).

audit.note: claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, prayed.vos.json only. Twelve readings, no unknown words. All are the Latin's own openness or already met by the rows: the objectless *Amei* (decision `dilexi`), the objectless *invocarei*, *inferno* heard as hell of the damned (the open row, D22; in the Office of the Dead the overtone is read on purpose), *pequeninos* heard as the lowly as well as children (the row), *fui humilhado* shamed or brought low (the Latin's), *repouso* peace or the grave, *queda* with a moral overtone (D44 foresaw it), *região dos vivos* this life or heaven (the Latin's, the Office of the Dead reads both). *Agradarei* possibly misheard as *agradecerei*: held (D44, settled). Nothing changed.

outcomes.reason: *placére → agradar* is settled (D44) and names this verse; a slip of the ear, not a second sense of the text.
